suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-11 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. In lung-transplant recipients with post-transplant pulmonary hypertension, chronic lung allograft dysfunction—particularly bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome—was the most frequently reported etiology/association, accounting for 63% of included cases. Use only for bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome/chronic lung allograft dysfunction after lung transplantation, with separately diagnosed pulmonary hypertension. Do not generalize to ordinary acute bronchiolitis. Preserve vascular/anastomotic complications, recurrent idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension, recurrent thromboembolic disease, left-heart/diastolic dysfunction, underlying transplant indication and other pulmonary-hypertension causes. The review calls for prospective longitudinal studies; do not state individual causation. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
